clinicalPearls: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by ELANE mutations in which neutrophil counts oscillate, typically with a regular cycle of about three weeks
During the nadir, patients develop recurrent fever, mouth ulcers, gingivitis, cervical adenopathy, and skin or respiratory infections
The characteristic periodicity distinguishes it from severe congenital neutropenia, which is persistent rather than oscillating
Diagnosis requires serial blood counts two or three times weekly for six to eight weeks to capture the cyclical pattern
Unlike severe congenital neutropenia, cyclic neutropenia carries little or no increased risk of leukaemic transformation
G-CSF shortens and shallows the neutrophil nadir and reduces infection during vulnerable periods
Monocytes and other cell lines often oscillate reciprocally, and symptoms tend to lessen with age
reference.pathophysiology: Cyclic neutropenia is caused by heterozygous mutations in ELANE, the gene for neutrophil elastase, which produce a misfolded protein that stresses developing myeloid precursors and periodically curtails granulopoiesis. The oscillation reflects a disturbance in the feedback regulation of the haematopoietic stem and progenitor compartment, so neutrophil production rises and falls in a regular rhythm of roughly three weeks. During each production trough the circulating neutrophil count falls to very low levels, leaving the patient transiently susceptible to bacterial infection and mucosal ulceration, before recovering as the next wave of granulopoiesis emerges. Although the same gene is implicated in severe congenital neutropenia, the mutational spectrum and cellular consequences differ, which is thought to explain why cyclic disease does not share the marked predisposition to myeloid malignancy.
additionalDifferentials: PFAPA and other periodic fever syndromes
additionalInvestigations: Serial full blood counts two to three times weekly over six to eight weeks to document the cycle
ELANE genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Bone marrow examination in atypical cases to assess maturation and exclude other pathology
Antineutrophil antibody testing to exclude autoimmune neutropenia
Inflammatory markers and cultures during febrile episodes to guide infection management
Dental and oral assessment for recurrent gingivitis and ulceration
redFlags: Serious deep-seated infection or sepsis during a neutrophil nadir
Clostridial or necrotising soft-tissue infection, a recognised hazard during severe nadirs
Failure of counts to recover between cycles, prompting reconsideration of severe congenital neutropenia
Persistent oral or perianal infection despite treatment
reference.prognosis: Cyclic neutropenia generally has a good long-term outlook, symptoms often attenuate with age, and it lacks the marked leukaemic risk of severe congenital neutropenia, though infections during nadirs can occasionally be life-threatening.
pitfalls: Making the diagnosis from a single blood count rather than serial sampling across a cycle
Confusing it with severe congenital neutropenia and overstating the leukaemia risk
Underestimating the danger of clostridial or necrotising infection during a deep nadir
Attributing recurrent mouth ulcers to an unrelated cause and missing the periodicity
references: Nathan and Oski's Hematology and Oncology of Infancy and Childhood
management: Use granulocyte colony-stimulating factor to shorten and shallow the neutrophil nadir and reduce infections during vulnerable troughs
Maintain meticulous oral and dental hygiene with antiseptic mouthwash to limit recurrent gingivitis and mucosal ulceration
Treat febrile episodes during the nadir promptly, taking cultures and starting broad-spectrum antibiotics as for febrile neutropenia
Track the cycle with serial full blood counts and adjust prophylaxis around predictable troughs
Provide genetic counselling for this autosomal dominant ELANE-related disorder and offer testing to affected relatives
Coordinate care between haematology and dentistry, with reassurance that leukaemic transformation risk is low unlike severe congenital neutropenia
